sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (training), Connect using the Windows Security Events via AMA connector
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. The connector 'uses Data Collection Rules (DCRs) to define the data to collect from each agent'; 'In the Resources tab, select +Add resource(s) to add machines to which the Data Collection Rule will apply'; Azure VMs and Azure Arc-enabled servers are listed; the Azure Monitor Agent is installed on selected machines; event levels All, Common, Minimal or Custom (XPath). The event-set reference page (learn.microsoft.com/da-dk/azure/sentinel/windows-security-event-id-reference, read the same day) says Minimal 'contains successful and failed user logons (event IDs 4624, 4625)'. The SecurityEvent table name is from memory of the Sentinel schema (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Wexley Logistics. Microsoft Sentinel's brute-force analytics rule alerts on repeated failed Windows sign-ins. Last week twelve on-premises file servers were onboarded to Azure Arc. This morning the help desk reports lockouts on those servers, yet Sentinel shows no failed sign-ins from them and no incident. The firewall team will only block a source if Sentinel shows it; their change window closes at 11:30.
handover: Security events come in through the Windows Security Events via AMA connector and its data collection rule dcr-winsec (event set: Common).
The Arc onboarding script installed the Azure Monitor Agent.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the new Arc servers, the data collection rule, the workspace and the analytics rule that reads it.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The firewall team's change window closes at 11:30, 75 minutes after the report; they block only on Sentinel evidence.

writeup.question: For the record: why Sentinel missed the spraying, what you changed, and how new servers are covered from now on.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: dcr-winsec applied to the 40 Azure VMs only; the twelve Arc servers had healthy agents and heartbeats but no rule association, so no security events left them.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Associated dcr-winsec with the twelve Arc servers; failed sign-ins arrived and the brute-force incident fired. Switching to all events floods the workspace without fixing the gap; lowering the threshold has no data to act on.

parts.label: From now on
parts.modelAnswer: The onboarding script associates the rule, and an alert fires for machines with heartbeats but no security events.

expertPath.text: No 4625 events from FS-ARC; DCR on 40 Azure VMs only; agents healthy; heartbeats present.
Associate the 12 Arc servers; onboarding script and silent-server alert.

flooded.headline: Associate the rule; do not widen it
flooded.body: The rule was fine for the machines it applied to. The new servers simply were not associated. Widening the event set multiplies cost and risks the cap.

sprayContinues.headline: No association, no events
sprayContinues.body: A data collection rule collects only from the machines it is applied to; onboarding an agent is not enough.

collected.headline: Good: close the collection gap
collected.body: You compared events by computer with the rule's associations, confirmed agents and heartbeats, associated the rule with the new servers, saw the incident fire, and made association part of onboarding with an alert for silent servers.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Lockouts with no events from those servers is a collection gap. The agents and heartbeats are fine, but dcr-winsec applies only to the 40 Azure VMs: the Arc servers were never added to its resources. Associate the rule with them, then check failed sign-ins arrive and the incident fires. Switching every machine to all events floods the workspace and still misses them; a lower threshold has no data. Then associate the rule in onboarding and alert on silent servers.
